title: Linking through unique identifiers in child profiles
description: Child profiles may contain unique identifiers (e.g., child ID, parent ID, or other unique references) that could be used to link data across different systems or contexts.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Child profiles may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., age, location, school, parent information) that could serve as quasi-identifiers when combined with external data sources.

title: Profiling of children through profile analysis
description: Child profile data could be analyzed for patterns to link data to specific children, potentially enabling profiling of children's behaviors, preferences, or characteristics.

title: Processing of identified child data
description: The system requests and processes identified child data for profile storage and management, which involves handling personal information about children.

title: Quasi-identifiers in child profiles
description: Child profiles may contain combinations of attributes that are unique to a data subject, enabling identification when combined with other data sources.

title: Data type sensitivity - potentially sensitive child data
description: Child profile data may include highly sensitive information (e.g., health, location, behavioral data) that should only be collected and processed when strictly required.

title: Excessive volume of child data processed
description: The system may process more personal data than functionally needed for child profile management, including unnecessary fields or redundant information.

title: Duration/retention of child profile data
description: Child profile data may be stored longer than functionally needed, creating privacy risks related to long-term retention of sensitive child information.

title: Personal data accessible to more parties than necessary
description: Child profile data may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary for the profile management system.

title: Unawareness of processing by data subjects
description: Children or their parents may not be fully aware of how their child profile data is collected, processed, stored, or disclosed.

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent in how personal data is processed or stored.

title: Lack of control for rectification/erasure
description: Data subjects may lack control in rectifying incorrect data or removing personal data that is no longer relevant.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data is processed than is actually needed for child profile management functionality.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Personal data is stored longer than needed, potentially violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for different data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) may be lacking for child profile data.

title: Excessive video metadata collection
description: Video metadata may include more sensitive data types than functionally required for the video management service, such as detailed user information, timestamps, or location data that could be perceived as highly sensitive.
assumptions: Assumes video metadata collection includes comprehensive user and video information beyond minimal functional requirements.

title: Excessive volume of video data processed
description: The MongoDB videos collection may process an excessive amount of personal data beyond what is functionally needed for the video management service, including video files and associated metadata.
assumptions: Assumes the system stores all video files and comprehensive metadata rather than minimal required data.

title: Data propagation to external services
description: Video metadata and files stored in MongoDB may be propagated to other services where they are not needed, potentially increasing exposure of personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the video management service may share or propagate data to other systems.

title: Unique identifiers in video metadata
description: Video metadata may contain unique references to the identity of data subjects (e.g., user IDs, account identifiers) that could be used to identify individuals.
assumptions: Assumes video metadata includes user identification information.

title: Revealing attributes in video data
description: Video files and metadata may contain revealing attributes that support the identification of data subjects, such as timestamps, location data, or behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Assumes video content and metadata include attributes that could reveal individual identity.

title: Unawareness of video data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their video data is being collected, stored, and processed by the Video Management Service.
assumptions: Assumes users may not be informed about the extent of video data processing.

title: Lack of data subject control over video data
description: Data subjects may lack control over how their video data is processed, stored, and retained, including preferences for data collection and deletion.
assumptions: Assumes the system may not provide adequate data subject controls for video data.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The storage of video metadata and files may process more personal data than is actually needed, violating the data minimization principle under GDPR.
assumptions: Assumes the system collects and stores more data than functionally required.

title: Linking through JWT identifier
description: JWT tokens contain unique identifiers that can be used to link user sessions and activities across different interactions with the authentication service.
assumptions: JWTs typically contain a unique subject identifier (sub claim) that can be used to track user behavior.

title: JWT contains unique identifier
description: JWT tokens contain unique references to the identity of the data subject, which can be used to identify and track the user across sessions.
assumptions: JWTs are designed to contain subject identifiers for authentication purposes.

title: JWT contains revealing attributes
description: JWT tokens may contain revealing attributes such as user roles, permissions, or other identifying information that supports identification of the data subject.
assumptions: JWTs may include claims beyond just the subject identifier.

title: JWT provides attributable data evidence
description: JWT tokens can be used to prevent an individual from denying certain claims about their authentication and actions performed during a session.
assumptions: JWTs are cryptographically signed and can be verified to attribute actions to a specific user.

title: JWT existence reveals authentication
description: The presence of a JWT in localStorage reveals that authentication has occurred and the user has been authenticated by the system.
assumptions: JWTs are stored in localStorage as a result of successful authentication.

title: localStorage accessible to predetermined parties
description: Data stored in browser localStorage is accessible to the browser and potentially other scripts within the same origin, which may be more parties than functionally necessary for authentication.
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to any script running in the same origin context.

title: localStorage data broadly accessible
description: Data stored in localStorage is publicly accessible within the browser context and can be accessed by other services or scripts, creating broader exposure than necessary.
assumptions: localStorage data can be read by any script in the same origin.

title: User unaware of JWT storage
description: Users may not be aware that their JWT tokens are being stored in localStorage, which is a persistent storage mechanism that may be accessed by other scripts.
assumptions: Users typically do not inspect localStorage contents.

title: Lack of control over JWT removal
description: Users may not know how to remove JWTs from localStorage, limiting their ability to exercise data subject rights such as erasure.
assumptions: Users may not be aware of localStorage contents or how to clear them.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing JWTs in localStorage may process more personal data than functionally needed for the authentication service's purpose.
assumptions: JWTs may contain more data than strictly required for authentication.
